C-BROWSER-CAPABILITY-GATEWAY-CONFINEMENT.Summary: Make one authenticated browser capability gateway the only path from features and browser services to engine and browser-domain effects, with truthful backend operation profiles, exact resource-target validation, real CEF semantics, and no silent no-op degradation.
C-BROWSER-CAPABILITY-GATEWAY-CONFINEMENT.Problem: The Astra audit found that CEF handshake and contract vocabulary advertise query, action, capture, and permission surfaces while the adapter returns Unsupported for important operations; reference S2 can mask the gap. Browser services also remain callable as domain libraries rather than being universally confined behind one production broker. Default or no-op adapters can turn missing enforcement into apparent success.

Goals.Goal: Publish a negotiated operation profile that reflects the selected backend implementation exactly.
Route tabs, windows, navigation, page observation, semantic query, semantic action, capture, permissions, history, bookmarks, and engine extensions through authenticated capability admission.
Validate context, page, frame, document revision, origin, operation, and activation epoch again at the effect sink.
Implement a minimum useful real-CEF programmable-page profile without raw JavaScript or debugger escape hatches.
Make unsupported, unavailable, degraded, stale, denied, incomplete, and backend-crash outcomes explicit and testable.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL DOES NOT APPROVE A PLAN OR IMPLEMENTATION.
The vNext architecture and effect-fence changes must be applied before this change is planned.
The gateway may be built for trusted callers before the untrusted feature host, but it cannot be published to untrusted callers until their isolation package is applied.
No browser service or feature may call CEF, CDP, native handles, profile storage, or backend internals directly.
Backend support negotiation must fail closed and cannot advertise operations implemented only by ReferenceBrowserBackend.
Semantic actions use typed operation vocabulary and revision-bound element references; generated JavaScript strings and unrestricted script evaluation are forbidden.
Permissions are decided by trusted policy projection and default deny; event subscribers cannot answer synchronous engine permission callbacks.
Engine-specific extensions are separately named and separately granted, never smuggled into portable operations.
Process-tree cleanup is availability containment, not proof of the CEF or OS sandbox; both claims require separate runtime evidence.
Search resolution remains separate from navigation and the approved browser-search plan remains immutable.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Full DevTools Protocol exposure to ordinary features.
Implementing every browser service or every engine operation.
Network egress, filesystem, credential, and download-byte brokering, which belong to a separate package.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The provider handshake and operation profile are derived from the selected backend and never claim support for an unconditional Unsupported implementation.

The common portable profile includes real CEF navigation, page observation, bounded semantic query, at least one typed semantic action, and bounded capture; any missing operation is explicit and absent from advertised support.
Each request carries authenticated caller, installation, runtime, capability handle, operation, resource selector, deadline, and effect fence across the private IPC boundary.
The authoritative gateway revalidates BrowserContextId, PageId, frame, DocumentRevision, origin, operation, grant scope, and activation epoch immediately before an effect.
Stale element, cross-context, cross-origin, cross-frame, and replaced-runtime requests fail with distinct typed outcomes and cause no browser mutation.
Browser service entrypoints cannot be reached by an untrusted runtime except through the gateway and their own narrower capability contracts.
History and bookmarks remain service-owned state with separate read and mutation authority; an absent bookmarks provider is reported as NotPresent rather than simulated by engine state.
Architecture checks reject direct feature or service dependencies on worldline-browser-cef, CDP, native provider internals, raw profile paths, or debugger APIs.
Default adapter construction cannot silently select a no-op implementation for a required policy or operation.
Runtime evidence records CEF sandbox enablement, browser and renderer privilege profiles, process roles, inherited handles, and failure containment separately from Job Object tree cleanup.
Real Windows CEF acceptance rejects ReferenceBrowserBackend substitution and records provider, runtime, CEF artifact, operation profile, and OS identity.
Provider crash or Unsupported operation degrades only the requested feature and leaves protected browsing, stop, and recovery paths available.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh real-CEF evidence proves truthful operation negotiation, authenticated gateway routing, exact resource and epoch checks, bounded query/action/capture, explicit unsupported behavior, and rejection of direct backend access.

Assumptions.Assumption: The current CEF adapter can implement a small semantic profile without exposing raw JavaScript or CDP to ordinary features.
Existing browser contracts can evolve additively through operation profiles while stable v1 fixtures remain readable.
History and bookmarks can remain independent service-owned state while using gateway-mediated engine effects and narrower service capabilities.
